analysis:
Examined scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py BASE lines 1–799 and the supplied bounded patch. Existing tests cover required-lane failure propagation (232–252), recursive checkout/build ordering (254–275), shard completeness and diagnostics, native media/retention gates, installer safeguards, credential exclusion, and cache-hit build enforcement (744–795). The visible addition at HEAD 155–187 introduces pinned checkout/cache action constants, a master/dev push-only cache-save policy, cached-.git connectivity validation with deletion on failure, sparse-checkout patterns, and helpers separating shared checkout steps from work steps. These are test expectations/helpers, not evidence that the workflow enforces the controls. No independently supported security regression is visible in this scope; neither runtime authorization, encryption, billing nor cache tenant scoping is changed by the supplied executable test code (relevant contracts include A-011/A-017, TB-003, TB-007 and T-041).
Integration must examine the actual .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml changes, alongside the omitted HEAD test additions identified by the range map (792–933 and 979–1007). In particular, validate restored-.git provenance, cache-key isolation, checkout credential persistence, and whether restored local Git configuration/hooks can affect checkout or later builds: git fsck connectivity alone does not establish their safety. Reconcile push-only cache writes with all action callers and confirm sparse checkout does not omit security/release inputs. These are unverified cross-file contracts, not findings against the visible test helpers. The patch is incomplete and no HEAD source excerpts were supplied, so this pass cannot establish the combined PR behavior.
